info.title: HR Platform API
info.description: Internal HR management platform — auth, employees, leaves, standups, projects, servers, payroll, profile, reports, and integrations (Google Calendar, Discord, generic webhooks).

tags.name: Goals
tags.description: Individual, team, and company goals / KPI tracking

tags.name: Feedback
tags.description: Peer, manager, and public recognition feedback notes

tags.name: Google Calendar
tags.description: Google OAuth connection and calendar sync

tags.name: Meetings
tags.description: Scheduled meetings backed by Google Calendar

tags.name: Discord
tags.description: Discord bot / Webhook Events integration for standups

tags.name: Email Settings
tags.description: Per-employee SMTP configuration for leave notifications

tags.name: Webhooks
tags.description: Generic inbound webhook endpoint for external services

tags.name: Onboard
tags.description: Public onboarding applications and contract review

bearerAuth.description: Obtained from POST /api/auth/login. Send as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.

status.description: Create only — 'onboarding' creates a pending applicant (is_active = false) awaiting approval via PUT /{id}/approve or PUT /{id}/reject.

discord_username.description: Update only — matched against Discord standup submissions

ip_address.description: Masked as •••••••• when is_sensitive=true and show_sensitive is not requested

ssh_user.description: Masked as •••••••• when is_sensitive=true and show_sensitive is not requested

email.description: Must be on an allowed organization domain

current_password.description: Required if the account already has a password set

token.description: Token from the reset-password email link

effective_rate.description: Estimated effective tax rate as a percentage

smtp_pass.description: Required on initial setup; omit to keep the stored password unchanged

password.description: Left unchanged if omitted/blank on update

nda_path.description: Stored filename of the uploaded signed contract

get.description: This endpoint returns a JSON object indicating whether the server is up and provides the current timestamp.

post.description: Use this endpoint to authenticate a user with their company email and password. The request should include a JSON body with 'email' and 'password' fields. The response will either return a JWT token upon successful authentication or one of several error responses if the credentials are invalid or the email domain is not allowed.

put.description: This API endpoint allows users to change their password. It requires a valid JWT bearer token for authentication and expects a JSON payload with the new password.

post.description: Request a password reset email that will be sent to the provided email address. The response always indicates a successful request, regardless of the email's existence to prevent enumeration.
Use this endpoint to reset your password by providing a valid reset token from an email and a new password. Ensure the token is not expired or invalid to proceed.

get.description: This endpoint returns aggregated data including headcount, leave, and project statistics. It is secured with bearer authentication, ensuring only authorized users can access the stats.
This endpoint retrieves an array of daily counts for standup submissions over the last 30 days. Use it to visualize submission trends.
This endpoint returns an array of objects representing daily counts of leave request submissions for the last 30 days. You can use this data to visualize leave request trends on a dashboard.
This endpoint returns an array of active employees in JSON format, useful for fetching and displaying employee information on a frontend application.

post.description: This endpoint allows you to create a new employee record, also seeding default leave balances for the current year.

get.description: This endpoint lists employees who have been created with the 'onboarding' status, indicating they are awaiting approval. It requires admin-level permissions.
This endpoint retrieves detailed information about an employee identified by their unique ID. It's useful for fetching employee profiles when you need to access specific employee data.

put.description: This endpoint allows updating the details of an employee by providing their ID and the updated fields in JSON format. It returns a success message if changes are made, or a message indicating no updates were needed.

delete.description: This endpoint allows the soft-deletion of an employee by setting the is_active flag to false. It requires the employee's ID in the path parameter.

get.description: This API endpoint provides a payroll summary for a specific employee for the current month, based on their salary divided by the number of working days. The summary includes details such as working days, approved leave days, present days, and the expected pay.

put.description: Set an employee's status to active and send a one-time password via email. This action is restricted to admin users and can only be performed on employees whose status is 'onboarding'.

400.description: Employee is not a pending applicant

put.description: This endpoint allows admins to permanently delete a pending employee record. It requires the employee to be in 'onboarding' status and includes an optional flag to send a rejection notice.

parameters.name: send_mail
parameters.description: If true, sends a rejection notice to the employee before deleting their record.

400.description: Employee is not a pending applicant

get.description: This endpoint allows employees to see their own pending, approved, or rejected leave requests. Admins and leads can filter by employee_id and request status.

to.description: If provided, sends a notification email via the employee's configured SMTP settings

post.description: This endpoint allows users to submit a leave request by providing their employee ID, leave type, start and end dates, and other optional details such as a reason for the leave and recipients for notifications.

put.description: Allows authorized employees to update a pending leave request. Ensure the request body includes the updated leave details and is sent to the specified employee ID.

delete.description: Cancels a pending leave request owned by the authenticated user. The request fails if the leave status is not 'pending' or if the user does not own the leave.

get.description: This endpoint retrieves an array of objects containing employee names, designations, profile pictures (if available), leave types, and end dates for today's approved leave.

get.summary: Get employees on approved leave this week

200.description: Array of employees out this week

get.description: This endpoint provides an array of objects containing employee names, designations, leave types, and dates for those on approved leave this week (Monday to Friday).
This API call retrieves the current year's leave balances for a specified employee ID. It's useful for frontend applications to fetch and display leave details in real-time.

put.description: This endpoint allows admins and leads to approve leave requests by specifying the leave ID and the user who approved it. It checks for date validity and ensures proper permissions before proceeding.
Rejects a leave request. Use this endpoint to reject a leave request by providing the leave ID and the ID of the user who will be approving the rejection. Ensure you have the necessary permissions.

get.description: Retrieve a list of standups for the current user or a specific employee, filtered by date if provided.

post.description: This endpoint allows you to submit a daily standup report for a specific employee. The data includes details such as yesterday's and today's progress, any blockers, and the date of the standup. This data is saved and, if configured, mirrored to Discord for team communication.

get.summary: Get today's standups (own or admin/lead only)
get.description: This endpoint retrieves an array of standups submitted today. Only users who are either the owner or have admin or lead privileges can access this information.

This endpoint retrieves an array of projects an employee is assigned to, including their role and milestones. You can use the provided employee ID to fetch the specific projects associated with a given employee.
Use the GET /api/projects endpoint to retrieve a list of projects, filtering by their status (active, archived, or on_hold).

post.description: Use this endpoint to create a new project with optional details such as name, description, repositories, documentation URLs, status, and dates.

put.description: This endpoint allows updating project details by providing the project ID in the path and the updated project data in the request body in JSON format.

get.description: Use this endpoint to retrieve a list of team assignments for a specific project identified by its ID. Make sure to include the project ID in the URL path to fetch the correct data.

post.description: Assigns an employee to a project and updates their role. This API requires the employee's ID and the role (lead, backend, frontend, ui_ux, qa, devops) to be provided in the request body.

delete.description: This endpoint allows an administrator to remove an employee from a project by specifying the project ID and the employee ID in the URL.

get.description: This API endpoint allows you to retrieve a list of milestones for a specific project identified by the provided ID. The ID is expected to be a valid integer.

post.description: This endpoint allows you to add a milestone with a title, due date, and status (pending, in_progress, or completed) to a specific project identified by the provided project ID.

put.description: This API allows updating a specific milestone within a project by providing the milestone's ID and updating the milestone's title, due date, and status.

get.description: This endpoint retrieves a list of service keys linked to a specific project identified by the provided ID. It is useful for applications that need to access or display service information associated with a particular project.

post.summary: Link service to project by ID
post.description: This endpoint allows you to associate a service with a specific project identified by its ID. You need to send the service key in the request body, and the server will return a success response upon successful linking.

delete.description: Unlinks a specific service from a project identified by its ID and serviceKey, returning a success response when successful.

get.description: This endpoint allows you to retrieve a list of servers associated with a specific project. You can filter the results by specifying the project ID in the query parameters.

post.description: Use this endpoint to create a new server. Provide server details such as name, environment, IP address, and SSH user to register a server.

put.description: To update a server, send a PUT request to the /api/servers/{id} endpoint with the server's details in the request body, which should be a JSON object. The server ID is part of the URL path and must be included in the request. The response will be a JSON object indicating success.

delete.description: This operation deletes a server record identified by the provided ID. It's useful for removing server data from the system when no longer needed.

get.description: This endpoint returns an array of the latest culture events. Developers can use this to display a list of events to users, ensuring they have access to the most current cultural happenings.

post.description: Use this endpoint to create a new event. The event can be a birthday, anniversary, team event, or milestone. You need to provide the event title, type, date, and optionally the employee ID and a description.

get.description: This endpoint returns an array of upcoming events in the next 30 days, which can be used to display upcoming events on a frontend application.
Returns an array of payroll records for administrators/leads to view all employees, and for other roles to see their own record only.

put.description: This API allows updating an employee's salary and pay frequency. It requires admin permissions and expects a JSON payload with updated salary details.
This API allows an admin to reset the password of a specific employee in the payroll system. The request should include an AdminPasswordResetInput object in the request body.

get.description: This endpoint allows users to view the tax profiles of their assigned employees, with tax calculations based on Nepal's income tax slabs. Access is restricted based on user roles.

put.description: This endpoint allows updating an employee's tax profile. It requires the employee's ID and a JSON payload for the new tax profile information. Admins have access to this endpoint.

get.description: Retrieve a list of goals for the authenticated user or filter by employee_id, status, and category for admins/leads.

post.description: Create a new goal for the authenticated user or assign a goal to another user with admin/lead permissions.

get.description: This endpoint aggregates and returns a list of summary statistics for each employee's goals. It requires a valid JWT token for authentication.

put.description: This API allows updating the details of a goal by its ID. It is intended for owners, admins, or leads to make changes.

delete.description: Removes a specific goal identified by its ID. Requires the user to have the appropriate permissions to delete the goal.

put.description: Use this endpoint to update the progress and status of a specific goal. Make sure to include the goal's ID in the path and provide the updated progress details in the request body.

get.description: List all or specific employee's performance reviews in draft, submitted, or acknowledged status.

post.description: Admin or lead users can create a new performance review draft for an employee within a unique review period. Request body should include necessary details for the review.

400.description: A review for this period already exists

get.description: This endpoint provides a list of rating points for a specific employee across their review periods. It requires the employeeId in the path and is secured with bearerAuth.

put.description: This API allows an admin or lead to update a draft performance review. The request should include the review data in JSON format. Ensure the status is 'draft' for the review to be updated.

400.description: Only draft reviews can be edited

delete.description: Deletes a draft review. Requires admin or lead permissions and only works when the review status is 'draft'.

400.description: Only draft reviews can be deleted

put.description: Used to submit a draft review to an employee. Admin and lead users only. This API is intended for integrating with backend systems by sending a PUT request to the endpoint with the employee's ID as a path parameter.
Acknowledges a submitted performance review by the employee who submitted it. Ensure the review is in the 'submitted' status and use the review's ID for the request.

400.description: Only submitted reviews can be acknowledged

get.description: Retrieve a list of feedback notes based on the specified scope and type.

400.description: Missing message or sending feedback to yourself

post.description: This endpoint allows users to send a feedback note to another employee. It requires a JSON payload containing the feedback message and is secured via bearer authentication.

get.description: This endpoint provides a list of feedback received counts per employee. It's useful for developers who need to integrate feedback data into their applications.

delete.description: Delete a specific feedback note by its ID. Ensure the request is authenticated with a valid token to prevent unauthorized deletion.

get.description: This endpoint retrieves the profile information of the currently logged-in employee. It requires a valid authentication token for authorization.

put.description: Use this endpoint to update editable profile fields. The request body should include the fields you want to update, and ensure you have a valid bearer token for authentication.

post.description: This endpoint allows users to upload or replace their profile photo. It accepts .jpg/.jpeg/.png/.webp files up to 5 MB and requires authentication via a Bearer token.

Use this endpoint to upload a front or back side of a citizenship document. Ensure the file is a .jpg, .jpeg, .png, or .webp file, no larger than 5 MB, and the file name matches the 'side' parameter (either 'front' or 'back').

400.description: Invalid side or no file uploaded

get.description: Retrieve a list of monthly reports by specifying the year and month in the URL query parameters.

post.description: Upload a monthly report in PDF, PPT, PPTX, DOC, or DOCX format as a multipart file. Required fields include file, employee_id, title, month, and year. The response is a Created object indicating successful upload.

400.description: Missing required fields or no file

get.description: This API endpoint allows users to download a specific report file by providing the report ID in the URL. It supports non-privileged users to access their own reports only.

delete.description: Deletes a report, only allowing the report's creator to delete it. This operation also removes the associated file from the server's storage.

get.description: This endpoint returns the Google OAuth consent URL, which is needed for OAuth authentication processes. It requires administrative permissions.

get.summary: Exchange auth code for tokens and redirect to frontend calendar
get.description: This endpoint receives an auth code from Google and exchanges it for access and refresh tokens. It then stores these tokens and redirects the frontend to the calendar page. It's useful for integrating the Google Calendar functionality after OAuth authentication.

302.description: Redirect to FRONTEND_URL/calendar with a status query param

get.description: This endpoint returns the connection status of the Google Calendar integration. It is secured with bearer authentication and responds with a JSON object describing the status.

delete.description: Stops push notifications and clears Google tokens, requiring proper authentication.

post.description: This endpoint allows you to manually sync upcoming Google Calendar events into meetings. You need to provide a valid API token for authentication.

This endpoint is triggered by Google to acknowledge push notifications for your Google Calendar integration. No authentication is required; it responds with 200 immediately and handles background syncs.

get.description: This endpoint allows you to retrieve a list of scheduled meetings from the last 7 days. You can use this information to display meeting schedules or notify users about upcoming meetings.

post.summary: Create Google Meeting and Calendar Event
post.description: Use this endpoint to create a meeting that will automatically be added to the user's Google Calendar with a direct link. The request body should contain the necessary meeting details.

delete.description: This API endpoint cancels a meeting by the creator or an admin, soft-deleting it and returning a 200 status if successful.

post.description: This endpoint is used to send a standup request to a Discord server. It requires a valid Ed25519 signature for security and should be used when integrating with the Discord API for standup commands.

200.description: Interaction response (PING ack or slash-command reply)

post.description: This endpoint allows submission of standup data for a Discord channel. It requires a valid internal token and includes the standup details and any blockers. The response indicates if the submission was successful and the employee associated with the standup.

get.description: This endpoint retrieves the SMTP settings for a specified employee. It ensures the stored password is never returned in the response.

put.summary: Update SMTP settings for an employee
put.description: Use this endpoint to update or create SMTP settings for a specific employee. Provide the employee's ID in the path and the SMTP settings in the request body. The endpoint will save the settings and test the SMTP connection if a password is provided.

get.description: Retrieve an array of stored service credentials for a specific employee identified by employeeId, ensuring secure handling of sensitive information.

post.summary: Create or update service credential by employeeId
post.description: This endpoint allows you to create or update a service credential for a specific employee. The employeeId is provided in the path, and you can include a service_name in the request body to update the credential. If no service_name is provided, the password remains unchanged.

get.description: This endpoint is used to verify the integration of a webhook by echoing back the provided hub.challenge parameter as a plain text response. It can be used by frontend engineers to ensure their webhook setup is correct without needing to make an API call.

200.description: Challenge echoed back as plain text

post.description: This endpoint is used to receive a payload from an external service or to respond to a Slack URL verification challenge. It always responds with a 200 status, acknowledging the request immediately. For Slack, it echoes the provided challenge value.

schema.description: Arbitrary event payload, or a Slack url_verification challenge

200.description: Acknowledged (or challenge echoed for Slack verification)

get.description: This endpoint allows your application to trigger a monthly report generation. It's used to integrate with n8n workflows, sending a request to n8n for generating and sending a monthly report.

200.description: sucessfully send data to n8n webhook

503.description: Error in sending request to n8n workflow

get.summary: Fetch onboarding form layout by type

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: Which onboarding form layout to fetch

get.description: You can fetch the onboarding form layout for either 'intern' or 'employee' by querying the 'type' parameter. The response will be a JSON structure grouped by sections.

post.description: This endpoint allows setting the form layout for onboarding. It requires admin or lead permissions and returns a success or error message based on the operation result.

get.description: This endpoint lists onboarding profiles based on the specified type (all, intern, or employee). You can filter the results by passing the type parameter in the query string.

post.description: This endpoint allows users to submit an onboarding application by providing JSON-formatted payload and a signed contract in binary format. The contract file size must not exceed 10 MB.

patch.description: Approves an onboarding profile by ID. Requires admin or lead permissions. Use this endpoint to enable access for a user profile.

delete.description: This API allows lead or admin users to remove an onboarding profile by specifying the profile's ID. It requires authentication via a bearer token.

get.description: This endpoint allows you to view the PDF contract file associated with a specific onboarding profile identified by the provided ID. The response will be a binary string representing the PDF file, which you can display or process as needed.
